DM Nisha Emotional Story | Heart Touching Hindi Story | IAS Officer Love Story | गरीब लड़के और DM मैडम की अधूरी प्रेम कहानी | Hindi Moral Story 2026

क्या होता है जब एक गरीब गांव की लड़की अपनी मेहनत और संघर्ष से DM Officer बन जाती है, लेकिन 5 साल बाद अपने ही गांव लौटकर उसे अपना पुराना प्यार ऐसी हालत में मिलता है जिसकी उसने कभी कल्पना भी नहीं की थी?

यह कहानी है निशा की, जिसने अपने सपनों को पूरा करने के लिए गांव छोड़ दिया था। कठिन परिस्थितियों, गरीबी और समाज की चुनौतियों का सामना करते हुए निशा ने अपनी मेहनत से बड़ी कामयाबी हासिल की और एक दिन DM बन गई।

लेकिन जब 5 साल बाद DM निशा अपने गांव वापस लौटती है, तो उसकी जिंदगी अचानक एक ऐसे मोड़ पर आ जाती है जहां उसका पद, उसकी कामयाबी और उसकी सारी खुशियां छोटी लगने लगती हैं।

जिस लड़के से निशा कभी बेइंतहा मोहब्बत करती थी, वही आज उसके सामने ऐसी हालत में खड़ा था कि निशा के कदम वहीं रुक गए। उसकी आंखों के सामने पुरानी यादें ताजा हो गईं और दिल में हजारों सवाल उठने लगे।

आखिर 5 साल में ऐसा क्या हुआ था जिसने उसके पुराने प्यार की जिंदगी पूरी तरह बदल दी?

snippet.title: How the Soviets Took Budapest
snippet.description:
From 26 December 1944 to 13 February 1945, the Soviet Union besieged Budapest, Hungary's capital. Hitler had declared the city a
fortress, to be held to the last. About 70,000 German and Hungarian soldiers (about 33,000 German and 37,000 Hungarian) were trapped
inside with some 800,000 civilians when Marshal Malinovsky's 2nd and Marshal Tolbukhin's 3rd Ukrainian Fronts closed the ring at
Esztergom. Hungary had been Germany's ally; when the regent, Miklós Horthy, announced an armistice on 15 October 1944, the Germans
forced him out and put the fascist Arrow Cross in power.

Three German relief attacks in January (Operations Konrad I, II and III) were stopped short of the city. In Pest, the flat east bank,
Soviet troops and Romanian troops (Romania had changed sides in August 1944) fought street by street. By 18 January the defenders had
fallen back to Buda and blown up the Danube bridges; the Margaret Bridge's Pest spans had already blown up by accident on 4 November
1944. Castle Hill held for almost four more weeks while food and ammunition ran out. On the night of 11 February, against Hitler's
order, the German commander, SS-General Karl Pfeffer-Wildenbruch, ordered a breakout through the Buda hills to the German lines about
25 km (15 miles) away. More than 20,000 German and Hungarian soldiers tried; estimates run from about 20,000-22,000 Germans alone to
some 28,000 in all. Fewer than 800 reached the German lines; most were killed or captured, Pfeffer-Wildenbruch and the Hungarian
commander Iván Hindy among the prisoners. Budapest surrendered on 13 February 1945.

About 38,000 of Budapest's civilians died in the siege, from the fighting, from starvation and disease, and in the Arrow Cross
militia's murders of Jews, many of them shot into the Danube; the memorial Shoes on the Danube Bank (Can Togay and Gyula Pauer, 2005),
sixty pairs of iron shoes on the Pest bank, remembers those shot into the river. The Chain Bridge was rebuilt and reopened in 1949.
In Farkasrét Cemetery in Buda, a memorial to the civilian victims stands in plot 19/1. Every February, around 13 February, the day
the siege ended, Hungary's National Heritage Institute holds a commemoration of the siege's civilian dead there; the 2026 ceremony
was the 22nd.

The numbers: Soviet and Romanian forces about 156,000-177,000 soldiers against 70,000-79,000 German and Hungarian, depending on the
count (DHM; Ungváry, ration strengths). The cost card counts civilians only: the soldiers' losses are published for different periods
(the Soviet figure, about 80,000 dead, covers the whole Budapest offensive from October).

Sources: Krisztián Ungváry, The Siege of Budapest: One Hundred Days in World War II (Yale University Press, 2005); Krisztián Ungváry
and Márton Ványai, "Mostly annihilated…", New Eastern Europe 1-2/2020, and "Kitörés Budapestről, 1945. február 11.", Clio
Műhelytanulmányok 2019/1; Karl-Heinz Frieser et al., Das Deutsche Reich und der Zweite Weltkrieg, vol. 8 (2007); Kornelia Papp, "Die
Schlacht um Budapest 1944/45", LeMO, Deutsches Historisches Museum (2015); John Lukacs, foreword to Ungváry's Siege of Budapest (2005); Nemzeti Örökség Intézete (National
Heritage Institute), commemoration of the civilian victims of the siege of Budapest, Farkasréti temető (2026) and Emlék-Őr (2020).

Maps and imagery: Army Map Service, U.S. Army, Middle Danube 1:100,000, A.M.S. M671 (G.S.G.S. 4416), sheets Budapest North and Budapest
South, 1944, Princeton University Library (public domain). Satellite: Sentinel-2 cloudless - https://s2maps.eu by EOX IT Services GmbH
(Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2016 & 2017); NASA Blue Marble. Elevation: SRTM (NASA, USGS) via AWS Terrain Tiles.
Borders 1944: OpenHistoricalMap (CC0) and Natural Earth. Farkasrét Cemetery outline: © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL).
Pictures: Marshals Meretskov, Malinovsky and Tolbukhin, 24 June 1945, and Marshal Tolbukhin, 1945, Ministry of Defence of the Russian
Federation, mil.ru (CC BY 4.0); Adolf Hitler, U.S. National Archives (public domain); the destroyed Chain Bridge, 1945, Fortepan 2048
(public domain); Buda Castle Hill and the Chain Bridge, Wilfredor, 2013 (CC0).

"Prelude and Action", "Clash Defiant", "Gathering Darkness", "Anguish". J. S. Bach, Air, performed by the Air Force Strings, United
States Air Force Band (public domain).

snippet.title: Why the New Atlas Robot Hand Only Has Four Fingers
snippet.description:
LEAVING THE PINKY OFF ON PURPOSE, Boston Dynamics gave its new Atlas hand four fingers and 13 degrees of freedom, up from 7. Each joint has its own motor, so a fifth finger would have added three more, along with cost, bulk and more that can break. The team tested the idea by taping their pinky and ring finger together for a day, and Hyundai plans to put Atlas to work at its Georgia plant starting in 2028.

I'd watch the direct-drive joints too. They make the hand easier to simulate, so grasps can be practiced in software first.

I follow stories and companies like this. Subscribe if you are interested in innovation.

Sources: Hyundai Motor Group, Boston Dynamics, IEEE Spectrum (Atlas hand)
